verdicts.reason: The quote is line 1 of the file word for word. The statement's first half (the answers are the interaction designer's, dated 9 November 2026) is exactly what the heading says; 'so the interaction designer is the authority' is read from the file being a ruling at all rather than from the heading's words, so the confidence would sit better as inferred. Sound either way.

The quote is the whole of line 3, verbatim. The statement follows: the note says the answers are to 'the design questions the waiting-on-design rows were blocked on'. 'that theme's blocked rows' adds the word theme, which the file never uses; harmless, but reconcile should not read a theme name into it.
'passed on by Sam the same day' is the tail of line 3. Sam as route and not author follows from that clause read with the heading's 'the interaction designer'.

Both lines are in the block quote at lines 5-6 (the '> ' markers stripped, the words untouched). The statement adds nothing beyond the pair heading's increment id. The note correctly flags that the quoted answer names no snagging increment.
The quote is the block quote's second pair, lines 8-9, verbatim. The statement reports the answer as given, without yet resolving what 'Same above' points at.
'Same above' is line 9. The inference is sound: the only answer above it is 'This has been picked up with the snagging list' on line 6, and the note names it. Properly marked inferred.
The quote is lines 11-12 of the block quote, verbatim. The statement narrows the quote's plural 'These' to amend, which the pair heading 'Amend pop-ups (inc-195)' licenses.

'they are now proper pages which should remove the issue' is in line 12. 'the issue that inc-195 was raised for' is read from the pair heading rather than the quoted clause, but the quote's bare 'the issue' has no other referent in the file.
'Designs can be found in 2.1' is the tail of line 12. Expanding '2.1' to Design Release 2.1 is read from item 3's 'The Design Release 2.1 designs', and the note says so.
The quote is lines 14-15 of the block quote, verbatim, and the statement is the first clause of the quoted answer unchanged.

'this unlocks this ticket.' is the tail of line 15 and 'this ticket' can only be the pair's own heading, as the note says. Flag for reconcile: item 4 (line 33) drops inc-162 rather than unblocking it, so this claim's 'no longer blocked' and claim 029's 'dropped' pull in different directions; the quote supports only the unlock.

The quote is lines 17-18 of the block quote, em dash and lower-case 'gov.uk' preserved. The statement is the quoted clause 'No need to add the type behaviour on top' restated. Note that the ruling's words are permissive (no need to add) rather than prohibitive, which matters when read beside claim 032.
'it should follow the gov.uk date input behaviour' is the second clause of line 18, verbatim, and the statement says only that.
The quote is lines 20-21 of the block quote, verbatim, and the statement is the quoted answer applied to the pair's own subject.

The quote matches item 1 at lines 25-26 exactly, including the line break and its three-space indent. Correctly marked inferred: the block quote says only 'This has been picked up with the snagging list', so inc-202 and the 'joined blue search button' description are the main session's reading, which the note states.
'and inc-188 went with it' is in line 26. Marked inferred with the implying words ('has been picked up with the snagging list') named in the note.
'Nothing changes. Confirms.' ends line 26. Correctly inferred: the block quote never says nothing changes, and the note names the 'has been picked up' wording it rests on.
The quote matches item 2 at lines 27-28 exactly, line break and indent included. Inferred is right: the designer's own answer is only 'Same above', so inc-204 is the main session's reading.

'Built in design snagging inc-204, which took in\n   inc-190.' is lines 27-28 as written. The statement's 'already answered by work that has been done' follows from item 2's headline 'already done' on the same line.
'Nothing changes. Confirms.' ends line 28. Inferred with the implying 'Same above' named in the note.

The quote is from the block quote (line 12), not from item 3 as the ref says, so the ref is loose; the words are in the source and the statement ('not a dialog shown over the page behind it') is the quote's 'no longer pop-ups ... now proper pages' restated, with item 3's 'not dialogs' on line 29 backing the wording.
The bolded headline is line 29 word for word. Correctly inferred: the note is right that the designer's plural 'These are no longer pop-ups' implies the cancel amendment pop-up without naming it.

The quote matches lines 29-30 exactly. The statement follows from the block quote's 'Designs can be found in 2.1' plus 'they are now proper pages'. One quibble: the words quoted are the main session's reading, not the designer's, so this is inferred rather than verbatim; the claim itself stands.

'which inc-120 and inc-121 (manage-notifications) build' is in line 30. Inferred is right: the block quote names no building increments. Reading the bare parenthetical '(manage-notifications)' as a theme is the extractor's gloss, which reconcile should treat as such.
'and inc-185 builds for\n   germinal products' spans lines 30-31 as quoted. The note is right that the block quote says nothing about germinal products or inc-185.
'inc-195, the dialogs over the page, is dropped.' is in line 31. Inferred, with the implying 'should remove the issue' named in the note.

'**No templates sort.** Design question 11.' opens line 32. Inferred is right: the quoted answer only drops templates and unlocks the ticket. The ref's line span (32-35) runs one line past item 4, which ends at line 34; a loose ref does not sink the claim.
The quote matches lines 32-33 exactly, backticks and line break included. Correctly inferred: the cross-reference to ruling:sam-2026-11-04 is the main session's, as the note says.

'inc-162 and its copy in the parked templates\n   theme, inc-248, are dropped.' spans lines 33-34, not 34-35 as the ref says; loose ref only. Inferred is right, and the note correctly flags that reading 'unlocks this ticket' as a drop is the main session's step.
The quoted fragment is in lines 33-34 (the ref says 34-35, one line out). Inferred is right: the designer's answer says nothing of a parked templates theme or inc-248.

I looked at line 15 ('dropped for now') and at item 4's 'If templates come back, the sort comes back as a question with them' (line 34, not line 35 as the ref says). The file gives no answer to the sort question and no condition on templates returning, so the silence is real. Empty quote is correct for a gap.

The headline and 'Design question 7.' are line 35 word for word (the ref's 36-39 is out by one and runs past item 5, which ends at line 37). Inferred is right. Worth flagging: the designer's words are permissive ('No need to add the type behaviour on top'), while item 5 reads them as prohibitive ('take no JavaScript on top'), so this claim is as strong as the main session's reading, not as the ruling's own wording.

'They behave as the GOV.UK\n   date input does: separate labelled boxes' spans lines 35-36 as quoted (ref out by two). Inferred is right: 'follow the gov.uk date input behaviour' is all the designer said, and spelling out separate labelled boxes is the reading.

'no digit filter' is in line 36 (ref says 38). Inferred, and the note correctly names 'No need to add the type behaviour on top' as the implying words. Same permissive-versus-prohibitive caveat as claim 032.
'no paste spreading' is in line 36 (ref says 38). Inferred from 'No need to add the type behaviour on top', which the note names; the designer never mentions paste.
'and no focus moving' ends the list in line 36 (ref says 38). Inferred, with the implying words named. The statement does not overreach beyond the item's wording.

'That is\n   what design snagging-b inc-219 built.' spans lines 36-37 as quoted (ref out by two). Inferred is right: no increment is named in the block quote. The statement keeps the distinct 'design snagging-b' theme name the item uses, which items 1, 2 and 6 do not.
'inc-093 is dropped.' is in line 37 (ref says 39). Inferred, with the note correctly saying the designer's answer implies the row is not built but never drops it.

'Each germinal date gets the\n   'Choose date' calendar' spans lines 38-39, not 40-41 as the ref says; loose ref only. Inferred is right: the designer said only 'Keep the MOJ date picker.', so the 'Choose date' label is the main session's reading.

'the Ministry of Justice date picker every other date in both frontends uses' is in line 39 (ref says 40-41). Inferred, and the note is right that the designer names the picker but makes no claim about every other date in both frontends.
'and\n   design snagging inc-206 styled' spans lines 39-40 as quoted (ref says 41). Inferred: no styling increment appears in the block quote.

'It is not replaced by the three-part date input.' is in line 40 (ref says 41). The item's 'It' is the MOJ date picker, so the statement's subject slips from the picker to 'the germinal dates'; the meaning is the same (the germinal dates keep the picker instead of a three-part date input). Inferred is right.
'inc-192 is released from\n   blocked to todo.' spans lines 40-41 as quoted. Inferred, with the note correctly saying the designer's answer says nothing about row state.

Gap holds. I read line 12 and item 3 (lines 29-31): the file gives only 'Designs can be found in 2.1' and 'The Design Release 2.1 designs show them as their own pages' — no page, screen name, file or link anywhere in the 41 lines.

Gap holds. Line 18 borrows the GOV.UK date input's behaviour for a county parish holding number, and item 5 (lines 35-37) lists only what the boxes do not do. Nowhere does the file give a number of boxes, box labels, widths, a hint or validation.

Gap holds at the ref given: line 9 is only 'Same above', so the designer's own words do not say whether the region code prefix was the same snagging item as the search buttons. The note is right that item 2's inc-204 beside item 1's inc-202 answers it at the reading level, not in the ruling's words.

Gap holds, with a caveat. At the lines cited (21, and 40-41) the file is silent on which germinal dates are meant. Item 6's 'Each germinal date gets the 'Choose date' calendar' (lines 38-39, just outside the ref) does answer coverage generically, so the open point is narrower than the statement reads: the file names no germinal date field and says nothing about a date range or an optional date.

Gap holds. The file mentions JavaScript only in item 5's headline about the county parish holding boxes (line 35); nothing in lines 20-21 or item 6 (lines 38-41) says how a germinal date is asked without JavaScript, even though keeping a picker raises it.
